Experience

AI Data Annotator & Frontier Model Evaluator

Independent Contractor
2023 – Present | Remote

At the leading edge of his technical journey, David works as an independent contractor in AI data annotation and evaluation — sitting at the precise intersection of his self-taught Python background and his long-standing instinct for quality assurance. His work spans a broad spectrum of evaluation tasks: assessing the accuracy, efficiency, and quality of AI-generated code across complex, multi-step programming problems; auditing chain-of-thought reasoning for logical soundness, computational efficiency, appropriate tool selection, and correctness at each step; and editing and annotating model outputs to produce high-quality training signal. A significant portion of his work involves rigorous system prompt adherence testing — not merely assessing whether instructions are well-crafted, but whether the model follows them precisely and consistently under varied, adversarial, and edge-case conditions. He stress-tests frontier-tier models at the outer boundary of their capabilities, surfacing failure modes, behavioral regressions, and subtle quality distinctions that feed directly into pre-training and fine-tuning pipelines for next-generation systems. It is demanding, nuanced work that rewards both technical fluency and rigorous analytical judgment — and it represents his most direct contribution to the field he is most committed to building expertise in.

AI Evaluation & Data Annotation

Through his independent contractor work, David has developed a specialized skill set in the evaluation and annotation of frontier AI systems. He develops and applies rubrics for assessing AI-generated code — evaluating correctness, efficiency, style, and adherence to complex specifications — and conducts chain-of-thought audits that examine the quality of model reasoning, tool selection, and stepwise logic at each stage. He evaluates system prompt adherence rigorously, probing whether models follow instructions precisely and consistently across varied and adversarial conditions. He edits and annotates raw model outputs to produce training-quality data, with a particular focus on the subtle quality distinctions that matter most when shaping next-generation high-capability systems. This work demands both technical literacy and the structured analytical discipline he first cultivated during his years as a quality assurance professional — making it, in retrospect, a role he was preparing for all along.
